common_ground.text: The old bounty overloaded engineers; triage should not fall to people with other duties.
Real, serious vulnerabilities should be rewarded.

output.headline: Whether and how Zcash should run a bug bounty now that AI makes spam reports cheap
output.next: Nothing is scheduled. thowar2 suggests leaving rewards for critical bugs to Coinholder Grants votes, with no formal bounty.

unresolved.text: How to judge which bugs between the obvious existential case and pure spam deserve a bounty.
Who should fund and review security reports: ZCG, Coinholder Grants, or a separate system with set-aside money and reviewers.
Can a bond or fee cut slop without pricing out good-faith researchers?

best_against.quote: It creates a real barrier that could deter legitimate researchers, especially independent researchers or people who aren’t already well-funded.

best_for.quote: Putting up a bond is not gatekeeping it is opening the doors to real reviewers. AI has changed the economics of bounties such that the cost of reporting becomes effectively zero while the cost of reviewing is high.

views.label: Make submitters post a bond or fee
views.one_line: AI makes reports cheap, so submitting should cost something. Rejected reports lose the bond, confident finders accept the risk, and forfeited bonds can pay reviewers.

best_against.quote: ZF and ZCG already had multiple people reviewing bugs and they were effectively DDOSed. The net effect of an unbound bounty program is that reported bugs will not be reviewed.

best_for.quote: Even HackerOne hires full time triagers whose entire job is this. Hence my suggestion to.... hire a triager.

views.label: Keep reporting free; pay a full-time triager
views.one_line: Do not gate reports. Hire a dedicated reviewer, or several on retainer, whose only job is triage, instead of leaning on engineers who have other duties.

best_against.quote: Many attacks have capital or time requirements that cannot be immediately replicated but a skilled, experienced triager can still see the benefit in them, which is why I advocate for a full time triager.

best_for.quote: Every submission runs in a sandbox against the affected release, if it reproduces the team gets called in for manual review with the evidence attached, if it doesn't run it's closed as spam and no engineer time is spent.

views.label: Keep a bounty, filtered by scope and evidence
views.one_line: A bounty puts many more eyes on the code. Pay for vulnerabilities, not bugs, and run each reporter's proof of concept in a sandbox so only reproduced exploits reach a human.

best_against.quote: I still think having a bug bounty is a huge net positive, because bounty hunters will pour a ton of LLM tokens, time, and effort into scrutinizing our code.

best_for.quote:
I believe any sort of bounty program will be gamed endlessly and is basically a waste of administrative effort.

Coinholders have proven that they will in fact pay out requested bounties for truly critical bugs at value adjusted amounts.

views.label: No bounty program; coinholders vote bonuses
views.one_line: Any bounty will be gamed endlessly and wastes effort. Coinholders can vote a discretionary reward for truly critical bugs, with no entitlement, and reject the rest.

output.why_it_matters: Zcash shut its bug bounty after spam reports. The thread asks how researchers get paid for real bugs, and who reviews reports, now that AI makes junk reports cheap.
